title: The CLI test helper doesn't pair --json and --plain by default, so a renderer divergence between them needs someone to remember to check both
description:
Follow-up from QCLI-272, filed per opum-agent's suggestion rather than folded into that (closed) task -- work discovered outside a task's acceptance criteria is a new task, not a silent addition.

QCLI-272 was a --json/--plain divergence: --json was always correct (JSON.stringify drops an undefined-valued property) and --plain leaked the JS value underneath it (Object.entries keeps it). The bug survived because most existing tests exercise one output mode or the other, not the same invocation through both -- the divergence class, not just this one mechanism, had no structural test coverage forcing both surfaces to be checked together.

QCLI-272's own new end-to-end test (test/qcli272-init-plain-omits-undefined.test.ts) asserts BOTH --plain (no literal undefined) and --json (both keys correctly absent) for the same invocation, but it does this ad hoc in one test file. The question this task is scoped to answer: should pairing --json and --plain assertions be the DEFAULT shape for CLI-process output tests, via the shared test helper, so a future divergence fails without anyone remembering to write the second assertion.

Not a decision to make on faith -- look at how many of the existing CLI-process tests (test/cli-tracker-process.test.ts and siblings) already call the same command in both modes with separate assertions versus how many only ever exercise one mode, before deciding whether a shared helper is worth the refactor or whether the ad hoc pattern QCLI-272 used is enough given how rare the underlying mechanism is.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A count is taken of existing CLI-process tests that exercise only one output mode for a given command versus both, so the decision below is made from that count rather than impression.

A decision is recorded either way: build a shared test-helper shape that runs a command through both --json and --plain and asserts on both by default, or explicitly decline to given the count, with the reason written down.
If built, at least the commands sharing renderHumanPayload's object-literal pattern (quest init and any future command found to use it) are migrated to the shared shape.
If declined, this task still leaves a written trail explaining why, so the next --json/--plain divergence does not have to rediscover the same question opum-agent raised on QCLI-272.

implementationNotes:
AC1 COUNT (measured 2026-10-11 in the repository, over the 62 test files that spawn the CLI entrypoint -- enumerated by grepping test/**/*.ts for src/cli/main.ts or a Bun.spawnSync of the CLI):

  only --json : 45 files
  only --plain:  0 files
  BOTH modes  : 13 files
  indirect    :  4 files (reach the CLI through a helper or a mode variable, so no literal --json/--plain appears)

So the DEFAULT shape of a CLI-process test is --json ONLY, by a wide margin (45 of 62), and a per-test "both modes by default" helper would touch most of them.

THE COUNT IS NOT THE WHOLE PICTURE, AND MEASURING IT CHANGED THE DECISION. test/cli-tracker-process.test.ts already carries a MANIFEST-DRIVEN harness (invokeEveryManifestPayloadCommand) that runs EVERY manifest payload command in --plain AND --json, in two tests, with the mode as a parameter. So "run the same command in both modes" is ALREADY structural for the whole command set -- which is why the raw per-file count understates it: those two harness tests are ONE file but cover every command. Separately, renderHumanPayload is not a narrow mechanism: it is the kind-agnostic FALLBACK human renderer, used for every command without a bespoke humanRenderer, so the QCLI-272 class is broad, not rare.

What the harness did NOT do is assert the thing QCLI-272 needed. It checked plain was non-empty and not the bare kind, and json had `principal` last -- per mode, with no correspondence between them. A --plain that leaked the literal word `undefined` satisfied every one of those, which is exactly how the divergence survived.

AC2 DECISION: DECLINE the per-test shared "both modes by default" helper; instead ADD the missing assertion to the harness that already runs both modes -- every manifest payload command's --plain output must not contain the literal word `undefined`. ONE assertion closes the class for every command, structurally, where a per-test helper would have covered one command per migrated test and touched 45 files to do it.

AC3: not applicable -- declined, so no migration to a shared shape.

AC4 (the written trail): this note. RESIDUAL AND ITS BOUNDARY, stated so it is known where it stops: the assertion keys on the literal word `undefined`, so a command whose LEGITIMATE data contains that word (a title or label reading `undefined`) would false-positive; none does today (the strengthened test passes over every command -- 420 assertions), and a future one would be a visible false red rather than a silent miss. It does not prove plain/json AGREEMENT in general, only that plain does not leak an unset field -- which is the specific class QCLI-272 was, and the one the harness's per-mode checks were blind to.

SHOWN TO FAIL WHEN THE DEFECT IS PRESENT, so the added assertion is not vacuous: deleting `.filter(([, entry]) => entry !== undefined)` from renderHumanPayload (the QCLI-272 fix) turns the strengthened test RED, printing `agentSkillSource: undefined` and five further leaked fields for `quest init` -- the exact reported shape. Restored, it is green.
finalSummary: QCLI-273 answered the --json/--plain pairing question with a measured count and a decision. COUNT over the 62 CLI-process test files: 45 exercise only --json, 0 only --plain, 13 both, 4 indirect. DECISION: decline a per-test both-modes-by-default helper -- the manifest-driven harness in cli-tracker-process.test.ts already runs every manifest payload command in BOTH modes, so the missing piece was an ASSERTION, not a runner. ONE assertion now closes the QCLI-272 class structurally for every command: a manifest payload command --plain output must not contain the literal word undefined. Shown to fail when the defect is present (deleting the renderHumanPayload undefined filter turns it red with the exact reported shape) and green when absent. AC3 is not applicable (declined, so nothing migrates). The count, decision and residual boundary are in the task note (AC4). Delivered on branch qcli-273-json-plain-pairing.
